title: How the show got the name Chocolate Kiddies
summary: A Hamburg chocolate sign gives Lyons the show's title, and the band's playing is the great surprise to audiences who had seen dancers before.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: But, one thing I forgot. As we came into the port -- we went on a British liner, LAMPORT and HOLT line, I think it was. I forgot to tell you, there was a big sign out going into Hamburg, saying 'chocolate', Swiss chocolates, choco-

And that's how the show got its name. Was the Chocolate Kiddies. You see, because there was a little kitty on there -- a couple of kiddies on there, brown skinned, dancing. And Lyons said, "That's the name of the show, 'Chocolate Kiddies'". And that quick, it was 'Chocolate Kiddies". Anyhow, when this was over, so now, they brought me because I was supposed to be the captain of the whole thing because I conducted them through the pit, went through with that alright, and then the band turned out to be the greatest of all the excitements. See because they had seen dancing before over there. There was Dora Dean and others had been over there as individuals, dancing. But, like Lucky Roberts was there with the Pickaninnies. And then Richie Wynn, and all of them, and Greenlee & Drayton, they had been over there dancing, see. But they had never heard these ten or eleven musicians doing what they were doing. So after it was over, Lyons said, "Well we're all going to take a party." I took a couple of the boys with me and Charley Davis and one of the boys and myself. And then Robbins, the music publisher that went over with us, Arthur Lyons, Goldberg, later on was with "Showboat" as a manager. For some reason, he claimed that he could handle colored people.
